chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who emancipated his female slave at the time of his death, so he said: Her waiting period is the waiting period of the free woman whose husband has died, four months and ten (days).

He said, And I asked him about a man who emancipated his female slave while he was alive, and he had already copulated with her, so he said: Her waiting period is the waiting period of the free divorced woman, three menstrual periods.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a female slave emancipated by her master?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal transition of a female slave (walidah) to free status, establishing that her waiting period (iddah) aligns with that of a free woman based on the timing of emancipation. If freed upon the master's death, she observes the widow's iddah of four months and ten days; if freed while alive after consummation, she observes the divorced woman's iddah of three menstrual periods. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic principle that emancipation confers the full legal status of a free woman regarding marital transitions.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who emancipated a mother of his child during the death. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Her waiting period is a waiting period of the free woman, the woman widowed from her husband, four months and ten (days)’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about a man who emancipated a mother of his child and he was alive, and he had copulated with her beforehand. So heasws said: ‘Her waiting period is a waiting period of the free woman, the divorced woman, of three Quroos (pure periods)’.
